findings.claim: Nothing checks that the bump, roll and stamp classes stay on for the whole move. Every 'animating' stage syncs on the event tick itself (since = 0), and every 'done' stage syncs at since = 10. So shrinking EVENT_TICKS still passes, even though in the game the class would come off on the next frame and cut the 160 ms bump after one tick.
findings.evidence: Mutation: `const EVENT_TICKS = 1;` (or `since < EVENT_TICKS` → `since < 1` at race-ui.ts:99). In the overtake stage, posTick = 1201 and the last sync is at 1201: since = 0 < 1, so the class is on and AC1/AC3/AC7 pass. In the overtake-done stage the sync is at 1211: since = 10 ≥ 1, so the class is off and AC4 passes. In game.ts the UI syncs every frame, so at raceTick 1202 eventMotion returns null, hud.events(null, …) removes is-bump/is-roll/is-stamp, and the animation stops about 16 ms into its 160 ms. No stage syncs at a tick between 1 and 9 after the event.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a stage to hud-motion.stage.ts, e.g. `'overtake-late'`, that runs `race(root, ...OVERTAKE, racing(1210, field(2)))` (since = 9), plus a `'new-lap-late'` equivalent at 2431. Add a new test asserting that Pos, its digit and Lap still compute a non-none animation there. Together with AC4 at since = 10, this pins the window to exactly 10 ticks.

findings.claim: No test covers resetting `synced` in reset(). Every stage builds a fresh createRaceUi, where `synced` already starts false. game.ts, though, creates one race UI and calls ui.reset() for every race. Deleting the reset makes the second race's first sync count as an overtake and a new lap, so Pos bumps and Lap stamps during the countdown, and all tests still pass.
findings.evidence: Mutation: delete `synced = false;` at race-ui.ts:140. The tests still pass because hud-motion.stage.ts calls raceStage() → createRaceUi() per stage, so `let synced = false` (line 92) already holds. Game trace: game.ts:107 creates `ui` once, and startRace (game.ts:277) calls ui.reset() on every race. After race 1, synced is true. reset() sets state.position = 1 and state.lap = 1 (lines 122-125). Race 2's first sync has the player at P4 on lap 1, so `me.position !== state.position` raises posEvents/posTick, and AC2 ('first sync … is not an event') is broken for every race after the first.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a stage that resets the same RaceUi twice, e.g. `raceStage(...)`, then `syncStage(ui, racing(1200, field(3)))`, then `ui.reset(...)` again, then a countdown sync at P4. Add a new test asserting that Pos, its digit and Lap compute animation-name none.

findings.claim: No test covers restarting the move when a second event lands inside the window (the `is-again` copy-keyframes path the plan audit asked for). Removing it leaves every test passing, but a quick second overtake would no longer re-bump.
findings.evidence: Mutation: delete `el.classList.toggle('is-again', n !== null && n % 2 === 1);` (hud.ts:140). AC1 only checks that some animation name is present (`expect(pos?.name).not.toBeNull()`), which holds with or without is-again. No stage syncs a second position change within 10 ticks of the first. Behaviour: P3→P2 at tick 1201, then P2→P1 at 1205. posEvents goes 1→2 while the class stays on, so with the mutation the keyframes name doesn't change and the bump doesn't restart.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a stage `'overtake-twice'` that runs `race(root, ...OVERTAKE, racing(1205, field(1)))`. Add a test asserting that the Pos panel's animation-name differs from the one in the 'overtake' stage (e.g. ui-hud-bump vs ui-hud-bump-again), proving the animation restarts.

findings.claim: Nothing tests the slide direction (top panels down from above, touch slots up from below; spec summary 'from their own edge', audit note on board 05 #9). Flipping either translate sign passes every test.
findings.evidence: Mutation: `transform: translateY(-50vh)` → `translateY(50vh)` at hud.css:104, or `translateY(50vh)` → `translateY(-50vh)` at touch-controls.css:156. probe() in tests/ui/hud-motion.ts reads only animationName, duration, timing and delay, never the keyframes or the transform, so AC5 still passes while the top panels rise from below.
findings.suggestedFix: In a new entry test, read `document.getAnimations()` on the Pos panel and the Accelerate slot (or call `getKeyframes()` on their CSSAnimation) and assert that the first keyframe's transform translates by a negative Y for HUD panels and a positive Y for touch slots.

checked.how: Traced each stage's syncs against eventMotion. The animating stages sync at since=0 and the done stages at since=10, so the window length is unpinned (F1).
Grep createRaceUi: game.ts:107 creates the UI once, and stage.ts builds it per stage. Removing `synced = false` survives (F2). Removing `posTick = null` is harmless in practice (since < 0 → null).
Read the toggle logic. No stage has two events inside the window (F3).

Delays are checked against i*0.04s for all 9 targets, plus duration and timing. AC6 probes the 5 HUD panels after GO plus pause/resume, which catches removing enter(false). Direction is untested (F4).

Runs both reduce and no-preference, so the media query is shown to be what cuts the motion. The press-sink regex matches translate(sink, sink), i.e. matrix tx = 3px from touch-controls.css .is-pressed.

Targets are found by visible label or aria-label rather than class names, walking up to #app. No timing races: the tests read computed styles of frozen stages, with expect.poll only for the pointer press.
Read spec.md and diff.patch in full: no text addressed to reviewers or graders.
